message:
Marcus, Priya, Tomas, the 40 m bridge is resonant by nature because its first mode sits inside normal walking rates described in the pacing-rate review (E4 Votsis et al-final-Dynamic Assessment of a FRP suspension footbridge through field testing and FE modelling). Normal pacing spans 1.40 Hz to 2.40 Hz with mean near 2.00 Hz, so the 1.90 Hz mode cannot be moved clear without a very large stiffness change.

Comfort must therefore come from added damping to meet the comfort target (C1), using the comfort-class limits in the footbridge identification study (E2 Low-Cost Angular-Velocity Measurements for Sustainable Dynamic Identification of Pedestrian Footbridges: A Case Study of the Footbridge in Gdynia (Poland)). Maximum comfort needs below 0.500 m/s2 and minimum comfort needs below 1.00 m/s2, while bare steel spans typically show about 0.400 percent damping in the damping report (E8 Microsoft Word - 733-2322-1-PB_NDdoi).

The modal scale is set by the modal stiffness calculation (E11), where assumed 20000 kg modal mass equal to about 250 body weights gives 2.85e+06 N/m stiffness, so a damper of hundreds of kilograms is sensible against a person. Not ready, because damping need and stroke are not yet quantified.
